local.title: Bello proposes 2027 budget that cuts the tax rate and funds a child care initiative
local.summary: But Monroe County Executive Adam Bello warned that the county is facing rising costs in several areas, combined with reduced or stagnant reimbursement rates from the state and federal government.
local.body:
Monroe County Executive Adam Bello's proposed 2027 budget would again cut the tax rate for property owners, his seventh spending plan in a row to do so.

The $1.6 billion plan would knock the tax rate down by 25 cents to an average of $5.42 per $1,000 assessed value. But Bello warned that the county is facing rising costs in several areas, combined with reduced or stagnant reimbursement rates from the state and federal government. His plan uses $33 million in reserve funds to offset those costs while holding spending growth below the rate of inflation.

"We continue to face growing financial pressure from unfunded federal and state mandates, and rising costs of pensions, healthcare and operating county government," Bello said in a release. “These growing obligations put increasing pressure on county taxpayers and are simply not sustainable over the long term.”

Much of the reserve funds are going to offset a $15 million hit the county took when the federal government changed certain reimbursement formulas for the SNAP food assistance program. For example, the county will receive half what it used to in reimbursed administrative costs, translating to a loss of $4.3 million, Bello said.

In other areas, reimbursement rates are not keeping up with expenses for services the county is required to provide by law. For example, Medicaid reimbursement rates have not kept pace with the increasing costs of providing care at Monroe Community Hospital.

And while New York requires its counties to provide Early Intervention and preschool special education services to children with developmental delays and disabilities, it has not adequately increased funding to do so, Bello said.

The budget includes $2 million toward a universal childcare trial program in Monroe County, which is getting $22 million from the state. Bello said that effort will add 1,000 childcare slots for Monroe County families with children up to 3 years old regardless of income.

And that cut to the tax rate — Bello said that was made possible by increasing property values in Monroe County and growth in the tax base.

local.body:
ORCHARD PARK -- The Buffalo Bills shored up their secondary by acquiring safety Amani Hooker in a trade with the Tennessee Titans, two people with knowledge of the deal told The Associated Press on Tuesday.

The people spoke to The AP because the trade has yet to be announced.

The deal was reached about two hours before the NFL’s deadline struck, and a day after the AFC-leading Bills improved to 7-1 with a 23-6 win at Minnesota. The Titans acquired Buffalo’s second-round pick in next year’s draft, and Buffalo also landed the Titans’ fifth-round pick, the people said.

Hooker is in his eighth NFL season with Tennessee and been a starter since 2021. He already has a career-high five interceptions this season, and is tied for the NFL lead with Green Bay’s Xavier McKinney.

The move improves a Bills defense that has struggled for much of the season, with the secondary singled out as being the weak spot. Buffalo’s depth at the position was further depleted last week after the team cut season-opening starter C.J. Gardner-Johnson because of his poor play and after he completed a one-game NFL suspension for spitting.

Hooker will be in line to take over the starting spot opposite Cole Bishop. Veteran backup Damar Hamlin started the past two games.

Tennessee, meantime, is in a rebuilding phase coming out of its bye week at 1-7 and sitting last in the AFC South. Hooker is the second defensive starter traded by Tennessee after the team dealt defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to Chicago two weeks ago.

A comedian who shared concerns about David Walliams’ inappropriate behavior with the British press fears she will never work in the television industry again after the best-selling children’s book author was accused of using his celebrity status to groom women for sex .

Lucy Beaumont, 43, told Sky News on Tuesday she was approached three years ago by a “young person” working in their first job in the industry, who had voiced concerns about the “Little Britain” star’s behind-the-scenes behavior.

“They took me aside and said ‘I need to tell somebody something’ and confided in me some of his conduct that they were really worried about,” Beaumont said of the concerning interaction.

Beaumont said the unnamed “young person” was required to take girls – who he thought were “definitely” over 16, the legal age of consent in the UK – to Walliams’ dressing room.

“The thing that struck me about it and that I was very concerned about was that he said they were very working-class girls, and some of them had never been to London before,” she said.

“They’d never been around TV. He felt they were vulnerable. This is the point of me talking about this because unless you do talk about it frankly, I don’t think anything will change.

“At the time, he didn’t think there was a process — a way to let people know within the TV company what was happening and how he felt, and I was really worried.”

Beaumont then said she was one of the people who shared the allegations with the Guardian newspaper – which identified the former “Britain’s Got Talent” judge on Tuesday after his lawyers failed to secure an injunction to prevent his unmasking.

entertainment.title: ‘NAZA’ Tops 1.5 Million Admissions Worldwide
entertainment.summary: Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor's award-winning exposé on Israel's war in Gaza has grossed more than $14 million at the box office to date.
entertainment.body:
NAZA hit a new box office milestone, with more than 1.5 million theatrical admissions worldwide.

The award-winning documentary from Israeli film-makers Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor looks at the alleged policies the Israeli Defense Force (IDF) uses to target and kill civilians in Gaza .

As of Friday, Nov. 6, NAZA racked up more than 1.54 million theatrical admissions across 47 territories, making it one of the most-watched theatrical docs of 2026.

The film premiered in Venice where it won the Special Jury Prize for directors Abraham and Szor. It was attacked by the right-wing in Israel. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called for the identification and prosecution of the film’s whistle-blower interviewees, and Israel’s culture minister threatened to strip the NAZA directors of their citizenship. Related Stories Movies 'Apart' Star Luca Pasqualino and Creator Stelana Kliris Unpack the Love Story Amid War and Apartheid Movies 'Bugonia,' 'Lord of the Flies' Among 2026 FilmLight Colour Awards Winners

In box office terms, the producers report a total take of more than $14 million, with $1 million and counting coming from the U.S., and $13.5 million in international gross. Michael Tuckman’s mTuckman Media intially started a self release of NAZA in the U.S. on Sept. 30 before Neon came on in late October to expand the film’s theatrical release.

The strongest performance has been in Italy, where NAZA bowed at number one on Sept. 29 via distributor I Wonder. The film has grossed more than $6 million to date, making it the third most-watched documentary in the territory, behind only Fahrenheit 9/11 and The March of the Penguins .

In France, where the film received a special 48-hours event release, to get around French windowing rules, NAZA sold more than 82,000 tickets, topping the box office over the two days.

The film has topped 100,000 admissions in the UK and Ireland, via distributor Dogwoof, and across Benelux via Cherry Pickers. It’s sold more than 80,000 tickets in Germany, more than 60,000 in Spain, and over 50, 000 in Switzerland. impressive figures for a documentary.

entertainment.title: ‘Apart’ Star Luca Pasqualino and Creator Stelana Kliris Unpack a Love Story Amid War and Apartheid
entertainment.summary: The film, starring Leem Lubany and inspired by the experiences of the writer-director's parents who emigrated from Cyprus to South Africa, opens Tallinn's Critics' Picks program.
entertainment.body:
South African Cypriot writer-director Stelana Kliris’ parents emigrated from Cyprus and moved to South Africa, leaving one divided country for another. What is that experience like, you wonder? Now, you can go on a cinematic journey to travel back in time and across the world to find out. Kliris ( Find Me Falling , Committed ) has used the experiences of her refugee parents as inspiration and “translated this into a film that challenges the idea of ‘us’ and ‘them.'”

Apart is the movie ‘s fitting title, and it stars Leem Lubany ( Omar , Rock the Kasbah ), Luca Pasqualino ( Rivals , The Musketeers ) and Girley Jazama ( Under the Hanging Tree , The White Line ). And with war and refugees constantly in the headlines, the film explores issues and challenges that feel particularly timely and topical. Related Stories Movies 'Bugonia,' 'Lord of the Flies' Among 2026 FilmLight Colour Awards Winners Business ITV Unveils "Temporary" Content Cost Cuts as Q3 Ad Revenue Drops 8 Percent Amid "Weaker" Demand

Apart will get its world premiere at the 30th edition of the Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival ( PÖFF ) in Estonia on Friday, Nov. 13, opening its Critics’ Picks section .

“In 1974, when Turkey invades Cyprus, young Eleni (Lubany) leaves her homeland through an arranged marriage and finds herself in Apartheid South Africa, swapping one divided country for another,” teases a synopsis for the film. “There, a new life with Nico (Pasqualino) slowly turns into love, until an unexpected friendship forces her to confront a secret from her past.”

Kliris wrote and directed Apart and produced it with Susan Simnett, Jamie Harvey and Ioanna Bolomyti. The cinematographer is Simon Sarketzis, with Emilios Avraam handling editing. Reinvent Yellow Sales is handling sales. Watch a trailer for Apart right here.

Pasqualino, who is now back on Disney+ in the second part of season 2 of the hit show Rivals , and Kliris talked to THR about Apart , how it was shot in Cyprus and captures a 1970s aesthetic, casting challenges, and how urgent the themes explored in the film feel.

Stelana, how much of Apart is based on your family’s history and experience?

STELANA KLIRIS My parents are both from Cyprus. My mom was a refugee from the war, and they actually met in South Africa. I was born and raised there. I experienced Apartheid as a child as I grew up during the ’80s in South Africa. So I grew up with all of these stories from both my parents and my own experiences. The film was an opportunity to bring all of that together.

entertainment.title: Placebo frontman Brian Molko snaps at fans in epic stage meltdown: ‘I’m talking to you, motherf–ker’
entertainment.summary: The singer was angered after seeing many concertgoers at his show filming and taking photos from the mosh pit.
entertainment.body:
Placebo frontman Brian Molko lost it with fans last week at his band’s gig in Milan, Italy, with footage of the meltdown now going viral on social media.

The singer, 53, was angered after seeing many concertgoers at his show filming and taking photos from the mosh pit at Unipol Forum, despite the band’s no-camera rule for their 30th anniversary tour.

Indeed, in the lead up to their gigs, Placebo had been displaying pre-show messages asking fans to put away their phones and immerse themselves in the live experience.

“You’ll remember the moment, not the recording,” was the message flashed on screens at arenas. Yet many fans have been sharing clips from the shows, regardless.

After performing their 1996 hit “Teenage Angst” at the Milan gig, Molko addressed the crowd, initially thanking those who had respected their request.

“We’d like to thank you all, well, almost all of you, for putting your phones away. Because in 1996, we didn’t have mobile phones,” he said from the stage while revealing he was suffering from COVID but decided to perform anyway.

“I’m here playing this concert for you, and you can’t put your f–king phone away?”

The rocker became more frustrated when only a few fans lowered their phones following his request, before shouting directly at audience members who continued filming.

entertainment.title: Foo Fighters star Dave Grohl invites Sydney fan backstage after wild Mentos stunt
entertainment.summary: Grohl then spotted a fan named Thomas brandishing a packet of the mints in the front row.
entertainment.body:
A brave Foo Fighters fan became the star of the show at the Foo Fighters stadium gig in Sydney when he bowed to frontman Dave Grohl’s demand to perform the Mentos geyser experiment.

During the rock band’s acoustic set at Tuesday night’s show, Grohl was sharing the long history behind the band’s “Big Me” music video, filmed in Sydney in 1996, which was a parody of a famous commercial by the candy brand.

“I didn’t eat those candies, because after we made this video, people threw those f–king things in my face every night every time we played this song,” he told 60,000 fans at the concert.

Grohl then spotted a fan named Thomas brandishing a packet of the mints in the front rows near the security barrier.

And he was not having Thomas throw the hard sugar bullets at his head.

“Don’t you f–king dare. I’m telling you, don’t be that guy!” the sweary rocker yelled, pointing at the mint man.

“How about this? I’m going to play this song and I want to watch you eat that whole f–king pack of Mentos while I’m playing this goddamn song. Keep the camera on this motherf–ker! If you can finish that whole pack before we’re done playing this song … I’ll chug a beer with you.”

Thomas took up the challenge. Now any citizen scientist, and Dave Grohl, knows that if you drop a Mentos into a carbonated beverage, it causes a sudden explosive eruption of foam.

entertainment.title: ‘Bugonia,’ ‘Lord of the Flies’ Among 2026 FilmLight Colour Awards Winners
entertainment.summary: The awards, announced at ToruńCamerimage in Poland, recognize color grading across five categories. Winners will receive a special full-color version of the festival’s Golden Frog trophy.
entertainment.body:
Yorgos Lanthimos’ Bugonia , Marc Munden’s Lord of the Flies and Hasan Hadi’s The President’s Cake were among the winners of the 2026 FilmLight Colour Awards, announced Saturday at the Toruń Camerimage film festival in Poland.

Bugonia , graded by Greg Fisher of Company 3, took the Theatrical Feature award. Lanthimos’ darkly comic science-fiction thriller stars Emma Stone as a powerful pharmaceutical executive kidnapped by two conspiracy theorists convinced she is an alien plotting to destroy Earth.

Aidan Farrell of The Farm Post Production won the TV Series/Episodic category for Lord of the Flies , Munden’s television adaptation of William Golding’s novel about a group of schoolboys stranded on an uninhabited island whose attempts to establish order descend into savagery. Related Stories Business ITV Unveils "Temporary" Content Cost Cuts as Q3 Ad Revenue Drops 8 Percent Amid "Weaker" Demand Movies 'Long Long Night' Director Youm Kyu-bock on Creating Animation That Takes Kids Seriously

The Spotlight and Documentary award went to The President’s Cake , graded by Andu Radu of Abator. Hadi’s feature, set in 1990s Iraq under Saddam Hussein, follows a young girl tasked with making a cake to celebrate the dictator’s birthday, an assignment that exposes the hardships of life under his regime.

The sixth annual awards recognize excellence in colour grading across five categories: Theatrical Feature, TV Series/Episodic, Spotlight and Documentary, Commercial and Emerging Talent. The winners received a special full-color version of Camerimage’s Golden Frog trophy, created in recognition of the contribution colorists make to the art of cinematography.

In the Commercial category, Nadia Khairat Gómez took the prize for the North Face campaign Defy Easy , while Imri Agmon won Emerging Talent for the Kidsuper SS26 fashion film The Boy Who Jumped the Moon .

The awards were presented as part of TorunCamerimage, the world’s leading festival dedicated to the art of cinematography. Festival founder and director Marek Żydowicz said the awards recognize the creative collaboration between colorists, cinematographers and directors in shaping a film’s visual language.

“Colorists help them achieve this, working together with cinematographers and directors to create emotional depth in film images, balance their colors and enhance color and tonal accents in individual shots,” Żydowicz said.

entertainment.title: The Lord Of The Rings: The Rings Of Power Season 3 Episode 2 Recap: Civil War In Númenor And Your New Favorite Orc — Grade It!
entertainment.summary: The fantasy saga's newest episode injects a streak of political drama into Middle-earth. Read our recap!
entertainment.body:
Ben Rothstein/Prime Video Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Season 3, Episode 2 of "The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power" shifts focus to explore a growing civil war in Númenor, which injects a streak of political drama into Middle-earth. The season premiere established the status quo five years after Sauron (Charlie Vickers) finally outed himself to Galadriel (Morfydd Clark), but this episode explores how the war has affected the wider world .

The growing rebellion against Pharazôn (Trystan Gravelle) feels similar to the kind of cloak-and-dagger spycraft that made "Andor" one of the best "Star Wars" shows . Gripping politics and backstabbing aside, Episode 2 also shines a spotlight on the orc Marnûkh (Adam Young) and his unlikely quest to help Galadriel and Arondir (Ismael Cruz Córdova) stop Sauron. Meanwhile, the Nazgnagôl throw a spanner into the works over in Khazad-dûm.

This chapter is a little slower compared to the action of the premiere, but it's clearly no less dramatic. Here's the low-down on all the biggest moments in the second episode of "The Rings of Power" Season 3.

Prime Video Episode 2 begins on Númenor, where a growing number of the population are secretly rebelling against Pharazôn's rule. Isildur (Maxim Baldry) makes it abundantly clear just how bad things have become when he tries to assassinate Pharazôn in his carriage, accidentally killing a woman instead. A second would-be killer also fails in the attack and winds up captured by the King's men. The attempt has Pharazôn rattled about the rebels, who are known as the Faithful — feel free to make your own joke about "The Traitors." He also questions whether Isildur's sister, Eärien (Ema Horvath), is truly loyal to him, because she was meant to be in the carriage during the assination attempt.

The question is answered when Eärien visits the captured would-be assassin, revealing herself as an ally before convincing the guards to kill him quickly as a small mercy. Then, at the Faithful stronghold in the Bay of Elros, Isildur is scolded for killing the innocent woman in the carriage. Míriel (Cynthia Addai-Robinson) teaches him: "Dividing the world into 'us' and 'them' creates a chasm that can only be filled by suffering."

Back in the city of Armenelos, Pharazôn and his cronies confront Eärien about her sneaking around in the hopes of getting her to spill secrets about the Faithful. Instead of agreeing to work for them, she approaches an open window and takes her own life. It's a haunting moment, one that makes it clear that this rebellion is about more than just politics. The episode ends with an ominous shot of the sea — which feels particularly poignant, considering the island's eventual fate ...

entertainment.title: Global Touring’s Growth Is Being Slowed By Lack of Infrastructure, Live Music Professionals Warn
entertainment.summary: At the 2026 Billboard Live Music Summit, live entertainment promoters and venue developers discuss the difficulties of breaking into new markets without more venues.
entertainment.body:
The number of touring markets continues to expanding across the globe, but live entertainment professionals believe the infrastructure has not yet caught up. With the advent of streaming, artists are able to grow their audiences far beyond their own country’s borders, but not all countries are able to accommodate the demand.

Across the globe, agents and promoters are having to book tours years in advance because the limited number of venues in emerging markets is so slim. Related Michael Sanft, Attorney Who Represented Keffe D in 2Pac Murder Trial, Dies at 54 Angel Diaz

“We really need more infrastructure from every country,” OCESA director of international events Guillermo “Memo” Parra said at the 2026 Billboard Live Music Summit today (Nov. 10). Mexico “was ahead of the curve regarding South America because of the Olympics and some other special events. Mexico had infrastructure. It was old, but they had infrastructure.”

On the International Touring Panel moderated by Billboard co-chief content officer Leila Cobo , AEG’s senior vp of global touring Angie Rho added that the promoter is looking to meet the demand in Asia, but is also facing a lack of event spaces. “You might have desire. You might have willingness. You might have fans, but we need venues,” Rho said.

Steve Collins , president of global venue development at Oak View Group told the audience that for every 10 buildings the company proposes, only one or two will come to fruition. Public funding for concert venues, Collins said, is not a popular model, so OVG looks into local partners in global markets to produce new buildings.

“Any market outside the U.S. is really tough to get these buildings done,” Collins said. “Whoever our partner is, you’re not going to take the risk. We’ll figure it out. We’ve become really good at commercializing these buildings and making them work standalone rather than putting our hand out as the first measure.”

Collins pointed to two music-first venues OVG is currently developing in Dublin and Madrid as examples. Both of these developing venues will not have sports tenants and therefore be purpose built to artists and music fans, as well as have more availability for concert nights.

Live Nation global tour promoter Nidhish Varughese said that the company has been focusing on growth in India, which has seen a series of record-breaking shows in recent years.

entertainment.title: Hilary Duff Reflects On Her Massive Lucky Me Tour: ‘I’m Really Proud of Myself, and That’s Hard to Feel As An Adult’
entertainment.summary: The current Billboard cover star received the Outstanding Pop Tour of the Year Award at the 2026 Billboard Live Music Summit in Los Angeles.
entertainment.body:
Current Billboard cover star Hilary Duff made an appearance at the Billboard Live Music Summit on Tuesday (Nov. 10) at the 1 Hotel West Hollywood to accept the award for Outstanding Pop Tour of the Year and talk about taking this run, The Lucky Me Tour, on the road .

Speaking with Billboard ‘s executive editor Lyndsey Havens , Duff reflected on the moments when she decided that she wanted to tour behind her hit album luck… or something, a run that brought her back out on the road after an almost 20-year hiatus from touring .

“I remember sitting with my husband and talking about it, and he’s always the person to calm me down and make everything really digestible,” Duff said. “But then past that I was sitting with my manager Darren [Gilmore] and Colin Lewis at Live Nation and being like, ‘no, I’m gonna do this,’ and just being really scrappy and confident, and then sitting in my car and being like, ‘oh my god, am I gonna do this?’ It was just one foot in front of the other, and then this other part of me that was like, ‘I know how to do this, and I know that I can.’”

Duff has more than proved that she could, with The Lucky Me Tour having grossed $48.3 million from 610,000 tickets sold through its first 40 shows, according to Billboard Boxscore. At the Summit, Duff spoke about how the show has evolved throughout the run, which will continue next year with 32 more dates in arenas across Europe, Latin America and the United States from May through November.

“We’re constantly evolving and changing things,” Duff said. “Like, ‘oh, that really worked this night, let’s lean more into that’, or ‘that song doesn’t fit well there, let’s change that.’ Constantly gut-checking what feels good and lands well with me is what makes it land with other people.”

Duff also spoke about the realities of being away from her four children while on the road, saying that “It’s been a real practice in like, I matter too, and my dreams matter too. It goes against everything in your body to step away from the children that you created. But it’s okay to make sacrifices for your family and still live a life that you find purpose in just for yourself. This has just been a big year of dreaming, and some of those dreams becoming realities.”

She also talked about speaking to her younger selves, from the era when she was a child star on a hit TV show to an internationally famous teenage pop star to an early twenty-something who stepped away from it all to figure her life out.

entertainment.title: Severe Weather, Radius Clauses and Finding the Next Generation of Festival Headliners: ‘It’s a Year-by-Year Fight to Stay Alive’
entertainment.summary: Huston Powell, Heather Kolker, Jeremy Shpizner, Melissa Ormond and Allen Scott in conversation at the Billboard Live Music Summit.
entertainment.body:
Within the last year, the festival space has experienced a more volatile market. Rising production costs and more frequent severe weather events have put events at risk, and at Billboard ’s Live Music Summit at the 1 Hotel in West Hollywood, C3 Presents ’ Huston Powell remarked, “It’s a year-by-year fight to stay alive.” Explore Billboard See latest videos, charts and news

Joined by Powell, Heather Kolker of Dreamshop Management, Jeremy Shpizner of booking agency ROAM, Melissa Ormond of Goldenvoice and Allen Scott of Another Planet Entertainment and moderated by Billboard senior correspondent Katie Bain , the conversation spanned how to determine a good festival headliner, navigating severe weather, rising costs and the best time to announce a lineup. Related Michael Sanft, Attorney Who Represented Keffe D in 2Pac Murder Trial, Dies at 54 Kenny MacPherson, Veteran Music Publisher and Big Deal Music Co-Founder, Dies at 71 Diddy Moved From New Jersey Prison to Similar Facility in Pennsylvania

For those looking to create their own festival, expenses have only gotten higher in recent years. “The inflation in the United States since 2021 has probably been around 27%,” Scott says. “For Outside Lands specifically, we’ve gone up 60% in our cost. It is extraordinary. And ticket prices can’t keep up with that. You have different price points and additional sponsorship, getting more top-end experiences to keep your general admission ticket price lower.”

Kolker added, “You can get into a situation where you get a festival offer that might make sense for where you are already, but with the cost of buses and crew coming out of COVID, it’s unaffordable.”

To help with keeping ticket prices at a reasonable rate for the average fan while still helping festival promoters make money, Ormond notes premium experiences are becoming more of a necessity. “There’s a segment of the population willing to pay for a higher-end experience, and that helps take some of the pressure off.”

Weather events have also led to festival cancellations. Bonnaroo announced it will be taking a year off in 2027 in order to let the grounds rest for a year following severe weather events in both 2025 and 2026.

“We have been dealing with weather conditions in New Orleans or Western Michigan forever,” Ormond said. “But California — we had never evacuated a festival until Cruel World in 2023. We had never evacuated the desert in 25 years of Coachella, and we evacuated twice in the last six months.”

entertainment.summary: “Please know that our absence takes nothing away from how much this recognition means to us," reads a statement from Sade.
entertainment.body:
It’s official: Sade won’t be on hand this weekend for their induction into the Rock And Roll Hall of Fame .

The elusive British act, fronted by the iconic singer Sade Adu , confirmed what should come as a surprise to none of their superfans, by way of a post on the band’s official website.

“Sorry we can’t be there in person to celebrate with the other artists,” reads the statement from Adu. “Please know that our absence takes nothing away from how much this recognition means to us.” Related Bella Kay Teases New Music In Billboard 'Up & Coming' Podcast Series Premiere: 'It's Kinda Giving Deluxe' It's Looking Like Oasis Will Skip Their Own Rock Hall of Fame Induction: 'It's Too Far To Be Going For the Night' Brothers Osborne, Luke Bryan, Vince Gill, Halestorm & More Added As 2026 CMA Awards Performers Explore Sade See latest videos, charts and news

Adu is tapped for Rock Hall induction in the performer category along with bandmates Paul Spencer Denman (bass guitar), Andrew Hale (keyboards) and Stuart Matthewman (saxophone). Sade will be inducted after their second nomination (the first came in 2024), in a Class of 2026 that’s stacked with countrymen and women, from Phil Collins to Billy Idol, Iron Maiden, Joy Division/New Order and Oasis

“Being inducted into the Rock And Roll Hall of Fame is both a gift and a timely reminder to give thanks,” Sade’s message continues, “not only to those who voted for us but also every single person who lets our music into their lives.”

The band also paid tribute to Australian artist manager Roger Davies, and the late record producer Mike Pela, who died in 2022, aged 72. ”We are indebted to the ones who’ve been with us on this road to get here,” the Sade message reads. “Sade, Stuart, Andrew and Paul. Mike Pela, the fifth Sade…this is as much yours as ours Mike. Forever our soul mate.”

Formed in London in the early 1980, Sade, all class and groove, slid into the airwaves with several of the era’s creamiest hits, including “Smooth Operator” and “Sweetest Taboo,” which both peaked at No. 5 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1985. Make no mistake, Sade was a leading figure in the second British invasion, only the group went to the top without the shoulder pads, teased hair or tabloid headlines.

Adu and her band have earned the reputation as one of the most enigmatic acts in music, with impressive gaps between albums. Sade’s most recent album, Soldier of Love , dropped in 2010, a full decade after its predecessor, Lovers Rock .

entertainment.title: ‘The Body’ Review: Despite Modest Blessings, Netflix’s Catholic Schoolgirl Horror-Drama-Satire Leaves Much to Be Desired
entertainment.summary: Created by Quinn Shephard ('Under the Bridge'), the aughts-set series follows a group of teenagers who set off town-wide hysteria after a dance team initiation gone wrong.
entertainment.body:
The girls of St. Marks Catholic High School are no saints. They spend their weekends drinking and dancing and hooking up at parties; they spend their schooldays gossiping and lying and keeping secrets. At one point, they invoke Satan as a joke and then seal the pseudo-ritual by dropping molly, unwittingly kicking off a chain reaction of events that will threaten to swallow their town whole.

If only the sins committed by their show were nearly as exciting. While The Body is not without its modest pleasures, they’re spread too thin over eight hours gifted with more ambition than effectiveness. In its uneven mélange of two-dimensional characters and underexplored ideas, the Netflix drama does a finer job of paying tribute to its pop culture forebears than of staking its own claim among them. Related Stories TV Catholic School Dance Team Wreaks Havoc in First Trailer for Netflix's Raunchy Psychodrama 'The Body' TV Netflix Sets Premiere Date, Drops First Look for Raunchy Catholic School Psychodrama 'The Body' The Body The Bottom Line Neither heavenly nor hellish. Airdate: Wednesday, Nov. 11 (Netflix) Cast: Kristina Bogic, Geena Meszaros, Sara Boustany, Jackson Kelly, Nnamdi Asomugha, Sofia Wyle, Shirley Chen, Orlando Norman, Louisa Krause, Gabby Windey Creator: Quinn Shephard

To TL;DR the premise, it’s Yellowjackets meets Carrie , at least to start. The tone is mostly straight-faced, neither bone-chillingly spooky nor bitingly funny, though it flirts from time to time with Emerald Fennell-ian excess and Ryan Murphy-esque irreverence , especially in the premiere directed by creator Quinn Shephard ( Under the Bridge ).

In the fall of 2004 — a setting you could carbon-date even without the caption by the velour tracksuits, Motorola flip phones and Balenciaga handbags, courtesy of costume designer Mirren Gordon-Crozier — the Lions, St. Marks’ all-female dance troupe, is holding tryouts. The team’s situation is dire: They’ve just lost a key member to injury in the weeks before regionals, and even the most promising of the new candidates, Grace (Sofia Wylie), is such a goody-two-shoes that co-captains Elise (Sara Boustany) and Anya (Kristina Bogic) disagree over whether she’ll be able to hang.

But the real trouble begins once a new girl is chosen for induction into the team. After a Halloween hazing ritual goes disastrously awry, the Lions are visited by strange visions and hard-to-explain occurrences that eventually blow up into a community-wide hysteria whose origins might be divine, demonic or just plain psychological.

entertainment.title: The Lord Of The Rings: The Rings Of Power Season 3 Premiere Recap: Sauron Corrupts And An Unlikely Ally Arrives — Grade It!
entertainment.summary: The epic fantasy saga is back! Find out what happens in the Season 3 premiere.
entertainment.body:
Ben Rothstein/Prime Video Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Season 3 acts as a soft reboot for "The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power," and the premiere wastes no time throwing us into the action. The previous chapters took their time building up conflicts in Middle-earth, but the third season kicks off with Sauron (Charlie Vickers) waging all-out war on the elves. It seems that this fighting has consumed Middle-earth in the five years since the end of Season 2, as Galadriel (Morfydd Clark) explains in her opening narration.

The sly dark lord was sneaky about revealing his identity during previous seasons, whether it was posing as the would-be king Halbrand or deceiving Celebrimbor (Charles Edwards) as Annatar, Lord of Gifts. Now that Sauron has put into motion his plans for the domination of Middle-earth, however, he refuses to hide, and he's more than happy to flaunt his true self — as well as that gravity-defying crown — from his home in Mordor.

Providing a helpful introduction to this lore-heavy episode, Galadriel's exposition also reveals that Sauron has begun corrupting the hearts of men across the land, even as the elven realms of Lindon and Rivendell hold strong against him.

Prime Video Sauron may be trying to crush Middle-earth in his steely grip, but his attempts to create One Ring To Rule Them All™ aren't exactly going well. The episode kicks off with him forging a golden band in his workshop in Barad-dûr — but he's smart enough not to give it a whirl himself. The crowd of orcs around him are also pretty uneasy about it; the show takes pains to hover on one orc in particular, Marnûkh (Adam Young), who shoves a slimy comrade forward to become Sauron's guinea pig. After a brief moment wielding the ring, the unfortunate orc's hand bursts into flame, swiftly followed by the rest of him. Oh dear.

Still, Sauron is clearly consumed by his quest to create a master ring. He even has Celebrimbor's decaying skeleton strung up on his wall, just in case it wasn't clear how evil he really is. For a brief moment, it even looks as if Celebrimbor's ghost is berating Sauron, telling him he'll never be able to make one ring capable of controlling the others ... or, for that matter, Galadriel. "The machinery of your soul is missing a piece," this vision tells him. "The one that allows for a true bond, a true union with another being. So, in place of connection, you seek control."

entertainment.title: The Chicks & Kacey Musgraves Complete Historic All-Female State Fayre 2027 Headline Bill
entertainment.summary: The country & roots-focused festival returns to Chelmsford, Essex, next summer.
entertainment.body:
The Chicks and Kacey Musgraves will join Shania Twain at the top of the bill for State Fayre 2027, completing an all-female headline lineup that organisers say is a first for a major U.K. camping festival.

Following its inaugural edition this summer, the festival heads back to Hylands Park in Chelmsford, Essex, between June 18-20. Twain was confirmed for the event in a post shared to State Fayre’s Instagram account on Nov. 2.

The Chicks, comprising Martie Maguire, Natalie Maines and Emily Strayer, will return to the U.K. for the first time since 2023, which included appearances at Glastonbury and BST Hyde Park supporting Bruce Springsteen. Musgraves will make her first festival headline appearance in the region, while Twain’s State Fayre slot forms part of a wider U.K. and Ireland summer run, which will see her perform in cities including Glasgow, Cardiff, Belfast and more through June 29.

State Fayre has also revealed its first wave of additional acts, with Billy Strings, Sam Barber, The Corrs, Drake Milligan, Sons Of The East, Brothers Osborne, Bear’s Den, Evan Honer, Noah James, Aaron Rowe, Mountain Grass Unit, Danny Worsnop, Taylor Acorn, Alyssa Bonagura and Bella McCormick among those confirmed. More artists are expected to be announced over the coming months.

Weekend and Saturday day tickets are available via the official State Fayre website . A presale for Friday and Sunday day tickets is now live via PayPal, ahead of general on-sale at 9 a.m (GMT) on Nov. 13.

In a press statement, State Fayre festival organisers Anna-Sophie Mertens and Alex Simmonds described The Chicks, Musgraves and Twain as “three incredible artists who each in their own way have inspired and represented vital change, within not only these genres but music as a whole.”

They continued: “To bring all three together as a U.K. festival first is something we’re very excited about. With further additions including in-demand Sam Barber, Billy Strings Brothers Osborne and The Corrs showing the breadth of what makes State Fayre what it is (and much more to be announced), we’re asking if it can be June 2027 already?”

Beyond the musical offerings, State Fayre will also bring experiential elements to the site including fairground rides and The Fume Pit, its dedicated barbecue area featuring more than 15 U.K. and international traders across the weekend.

entertainment.title: Agents Look Ahead as AI Keeps Advancing: ‘We Have the Privilege of Being in a Human Industry’
entertainment.summary: Jbeau Lewis, Cristina Baxter, Robby Fraser, Jarred Arfa, Josh Mulder and Shirin Nury joined the conversation at the 2026 Billboard Live Music Summit.
entertainment.body:
Agents Jbeau Lewis of UTA , Cristina Baxter of THE•TEAM, Robby Fraser of WME , Jarred Arfa of Independent Artists Group, Josh Mulder of TBA and Shirin Nury of CAA joined the Billboard Live Music Summit at the 1 Hotel in West Hollywood, California, on Tuesday (Nov. 10). Explore Billboard See latest videos, charts and news

Moderated by Billboard senior editor Taylor Mims , the panel spanned how the middle class of touring has been getting squeezed in recent years, rising production costs, smart tour packaging, and how far in advance tours are being booked. Related Michael Sanft, Attorney Who Represented Keffe D in 2Pac Murder Trial, Dies at 54 Kenny MacPherson, Veteran Music Publisher and Big Deal Music Co-Founder, Dies at 71 Diddy Moved From New Jersey Prison to Similar Facility in Pennsylvania

Baxter spoke of how rising tour costs and larger production has created a fine line on becoming profitable, with artists wanting to present their all but needing to be mindful of budget. For artists performing clubs and theaters, those challenges are even more apparent.

“The margins are just so razor thin now,” Baxter says. “Whether a tour is profitable or not and becomes a successful, sold-out tour, can come down to just a couple of decisions, such as the number of days and the cost of a certain element in production.”

Arfa added, “There are situations when making money may not even be the goal. Maybe an artist is trying to ascend to a new level, and the conversations are how to break even.”

As ticket prices continue to rise, those on the panel also noted that concerts may be considered a more luxury experience. Following the COVID pandemic, touring experienced a boom with more artists on the road and more tickets sold than ever before. Now, those in the live industry are seeing that growth has begun to slow, with 2024 and 2025 experiencing a plateau in ticket gross, according to Billboard ’s 2025 year-end touring report .

“There’s been a sea-change in our business post pandemic,” Lewis said. “We saw a dramatic rise and change in the model and behavior of consumers. Expecting it to rise consistently is unrealistic. I think we’re probably there now.”

Despite this, tours are being booked further in advance, with some agents already looking to 2028 and 2029. As they look ahead, agents note the need for flexibility.

entertainment.summary: The pioneering DJ and record producer was honored during a ceremony at Windsor Castle.
entertainment.body:
Oh yes, oh yes! Carl Cox has been presented with his OBE (Officer of the Order of the British Empire), with Prince William on royal duties.

The pioneering British DJ and record producer is recognized for his outstanding services to music, and was one of several music figures identified in the King’s Birthday Honours List back in June of this year.

King Charles’ first born, William, had the honor of presenting Cox with his award during a ceremony this week at Windsor Castle. Related Bella Kay Teases New Music In Billboard 'Up & Coming' Podcast Series Premiere: 'It's Kinda Giving Deluxe' It's Looking Like Oasis Will Skip Their Own Rock Hall of Fame Induction: 'It's Too Far To Be Going For the Night' Brothers Osborne, Luke Bryan, Vince Gill, Halestorm & More Added As 2026 CMA Awards Performers Explore Carl Cox See latest videos, charts and news

“I’m not quite sure I can put into words what today means to me,” Cox writes on his social channels. “Music has been my whole life. From those early days of falling in love with records and DJing, to travelling the world and sharing that love with so many people, I’ve never stopped being grateful that I get to do what I do.”

To receive his OBE from Prince William at Windsor Castle, “recognising nearly 50 years of doing something I absolutely love,” Cox writes, “is beyond anything I could have imagined.”

Cox isn’t just a DJ. He’s an institution, an integral part of the house and techno electronic music story, one of the first “superstar” DJs and a vinyl technician who mastered the three-deck and four-deck mixing techniques. He founded his label Intec Records in 1999, and is a familiar face behind the decks at the biggest festivals and clubs, everywhere.

As clubland remained in lockdown during the pandemic, Cox used the time wisely to complete his autobiography, “Oh Yes, Oh Yes!,” a reference to his catchphrase. The book dropped in August 2021, published by White Rabbit.

“This honour means so much, not just to me personally, but because of where our music has come from and how far it has travelled. To see dance music recognised in this way is something I’m immensely proud of.”

entertainment.title: VisionQuest's Finale Brings Back More Than One Familiar MCU Face — Grade The Episode (And That Mid-Credits Surprise!)

Disney+ Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover The following post contains spoilers for the "VisionQuest" finale.

With all due respect to Vision, the finale of his own TV show is all about the Maximoffs.

The "WandaVision" trilogy — which includes that series, "Agatha All Along," and the presently concluding "VisionQuest" — has long been hinting at the possibility of a family reunion for Wanda, Vision, and their twin sons, even when the prospect of getting that foursome back together has seemed impossible. After all, Wanda appeared to perish during "Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness," and the MCU has thus far stuck to that story, even when fans have hoped it wouldn't.

But Tuesday's "VisionQuest" closer not only brings back Joe Locke as Billy Maximoff (first seen in "Agatha All Along"), but, yes indeed, Elizabeth Olsen as Wanda Maximoff, who is resurrected in the final second of the final scene of the final episode. (It's been a while since a mid-credits Marvel scene carried such weight, eh?)

Let's get into the specifics of "Forever," then we'll want to hear your thoughts on the finale in the comments.

Disney+ We pick up at Horton Manor, where we learn that Paladin's mysterious client is Virgil Horton (James Spader in a different role), grandson of Phineas Horton and ex-husband of Jocasta. Virgil is holding Vision and Jocasta captive, but he's also hosting them for dinner while offering the audience some of his own backstory: His grandfather's Synthetic Man creation famously went up in flames, and his mother died penniless, left with only a journal full of Phineas' old code that Virgil later inherited. The code was a solid foundation for AI technology, though, and once Virgil married Jocasta, they used their minds "to make the artificial real."

After Jocasta died several years ago — around the same time that Vision was in pieces post-"Infinity War" — Virgil took a classified job at S.W.O.R.D., and he was the person who rebuilt Vision as the White Vision introduced to us in "WandaVision". At S.W.O.R.D., Virgil also siphoned materials to rebuild Jocasta, but he believes himself unworthy to be Jocasta's partner in crime in her new, more powerful form. "How could you possibly love me?" Virgil tells his robot ex at his dinner table. "You're a goddess now. A goddess who deserves her god."

That's where Vision comes into Virgil's plan. Virgil wants to upload his brilliant consciousness into a different, better-equipped body so that he and Jocasta can rule the world together. And Vision? He's "the perfect vessel," Virgil says. Vision realizes that this is why Virgil put a bounty on his head in the first place: "In an attempt to avoid loss, you hired the Paladin to find me, to use me as a vessel," Vision says. " Your mind, this body."

entertainment.body:
A new take on the beloved rom-com You’ve Got Mail is in the works at Warner Bros ., The Hollywood Reporter has learned.

Rather than a remake of the original 1998 film starring Tom Hanks and Meg Ryan, the new film will follow a new story, though plot details are being kept under wraps.

Jason Orley ( Close Personal Friends , Bupkis and I Want You Back ) has been tapped to direct the project. He’s also writing the current draft based on a screenplay by Deborah Kaplan and Harry Elfont. Neal Moritz and Tania Landau from the original movie are also returning to produce. Related Stories Business Pam Abdy Laments Exits of Top Female Executives in Hollywood: "It Is Upsetting to See" Movies DC Studios' James Gunn and Peter Safran Recall Detailing Long-Term Plans to New Boss David Ellison

The 1998 pic, based on Miklós László’s 1937 Hungarian play Parfumerie , follows book superstore magnate Joe Fox (Hanks) and independent book shop owner Kathleen Kelly (Ryan) as they fall in love in the anonymity of the Internet. However, they’re both blissfully unaware that he’s trying to put her out of business. Greg Kinnear, Parker Posey, Jean Stapleton, Steve Zahn, Heather Burns and Dave Chappelle also starred in the film helmed by Nora Ephron.

Upon its release, You’ve Got Mail grossed more than $250 million at the global box office, not adjusted for inflation. It became Ephron’s highest-grossing film to date, behind Sleepless in Seattle (1993). Ryan also earned a Golden Globe nomination the following year for best actress in a motion picture — comedy or musical for her performance as Kathleen.

Orley is repped by UTA, Rise Management and Hansen, Jacobson, Teller, Hoberman, Newman, Warren, Richman, Rush, Kaller, & Gellman L.L.P.

entertainment.title: Jack River Signs With G.Y.R.O., Releases First New Music In Three Years
entertainment.summary: “Borderline” is Jack River’s first release since 2023’s "Endless Summer."
entertainment.body:
The independent Australian singer, songwriter and advocate (real name: Holly Rankin) returns with a new deal via G.Y.R.O. (Get Your Record Out), and new music in “Borderline.”

A lowkey electronic earworm, “Borderline” is Jack River’s first release since 2023’s Endless Summer , during which she performed over 20 shows while pregnant with her first daughter Maggie. Explore Jack River See latest videos, charts and news

“Borderline” was written following her breakthrough night out on her own, capturing the emotions, the fears, the vulnerability and the strength that comes with rediscovering the world. Related Bella Kay Teases New Music In Billboard 'Up & Coming' Podcast Series Premiere: 'It's Kinda Giving Deluxe' It's Looking Like Oasis Will Skip Their Own Rock Hall of Fame Induction: 'It's Too Far To Be Going For the Night' Brothers Osborne, Luke Bryan, Vince Gill, Halestorm & More Added As 2026 CMA Awards Performers

“This is a song about traveling beyond the borderline, back to one’s self, back to freedom,” she explains. “I wrote this song after one of my first nights alone in three years, overwhelmed with the feeling that my sense of self was returning, and the reckoning that comes with that. It’s the beginning of a new era for Jack River – with less rules, less constraints, and more independence.”

There’s more on the way. Rankin is hard at work on a collection of songs which will traverse those years of “change and transition,” in her “relationships, her career and her personal world,” reads a statement announcing the new project. “Motherhood brought fearlessness, conviction and a realization that there’s no time to mess around, bringing with it new discipline and boundaries, but also a sense of freedom.”

Jack River established her as one of the Australian music scene’s leading lights with her 2018 debut album Sugar Mountain , which snagged three ARIA Award nominations (breakthrough artist of the year, best pop release and engineer of the year), an AIR Award nomination (best independent pop album) and an APRA Award nomination (breakthrough songwriter of the year).

Andy Irvine, CEO and co-founder of G.Y.R.O., the Brisbane-based independent music distribution and label services specialist, welcomes Jack River to its roster. “Holly has a clear vision for her music and an unwavering determination to make the Australian industry better for artists,” he remarks. “The team at G.Y.R.O. are excited to harness that independent spirit and bring her new music to audiences here and around the world.”

entertainment.summary: Prince George is displaying a crowning achievement. The eldest son of Prince William and Kate Middleton showed off his immense artist talent in an upcoming issue of Country Life magazine,...
entertainment.body:
The eldest son of Prince William and Kate Middleton showed off his immense artist talent in an upcoming issue of Country Life magazine, guest-edited by his father, with a drawing of a kingfisher done by the 13-year-old.

George’s drawing features the bird with dark green and yellow plumage—and the signature pointed bill of a kingfisher—perched on top of a piece of wood, gazing off into the distance.

And he’s had a knack for the arts for years. Back in 2022, he drew a portrait of a reindeer that his family—including siblings Princess Charlotte , 11, and Prince Louis , 8—shared as their Christmas card on Instagram that year .

It's no wonder that he has picked up a palette, as both his mother and his grandfather King Charles III are quite artistically inclined as well. Kate received her degree in art history and has previously displayed her skills, posting a sketch of St. Andrews in Scotland in 2021 as well as photographing the royal family over the years . Charles, meanwhile, is known for his landscapes, often depicting Balmoral Castle in Scotland, Windsor Castle and other royal properties.

As for Kate, she shared a look at the whole family’s art skills in 2025, posting portraits she and her children had drawn to Instagram that had provided “a moment of connection”—although she did not say who had drawn which portrait.

In recent months George has been keeping busy not only with art but also as a student at Eton College while he prepares to one day take the throne following his grandfather and father.

"There’s lots of things to think about with that," William noted on an October episode of The Reluctant Traveler With Eugene Levy . "But obviously, I want to create a world in which my son is proud of what we do and a world and a job that actually does impact people’s lives for the better.”

And much of that desire comes from what he and brother Prince Harry experienced during their childhoods, adding, "That is caveated with I hope we don’t go back to some of the practices in the past that Harry and I had to grow up in. And I’ll do everything I can to make sure we don’t regress in that situation."

entertainment.title: Why Florence Pugh Is Done Tolerating “Bullsh** Behavior” on Set: “Don’t Be Rude”
entertainment.summary: The 'East of Eden' actress opens up about how she's become "more confident in the way that I can protect myself" when working in Hollywood.
entertainment.body:
Don’t mess with Florence Pugh on a film set because she’s “not standing for bullshit behavior” anymore.

The Oscar-nominated actress got candid during a recent interview with Elle magazine about what she’s learned throughout the last 12 years working in Hollywood. After making her film debut in 2014’s The Falling , Pugh has grown to become one of the most prominent actors in the industry, starring in top projects from Midsommar and Oppenheimer to Thunderbolts* and the Dune franchise.

“The thing that I’m getting better and better at is protecting myself,” she admitted. “Every time I work on a movie, I get more confident in the way that I can protect myself and the way that I can lead a film set, and just not stand for bullshit anymore. I’m not doing it. I’m not standing for bullshit behavior. I’m not standing for bullshit attitude. I’m not allowing for people to be rude to the crew.” Related Stories Beyond the Book Free IP and Fresh Eyes: How Hollywood Is Reinventing the Classics TV 'East of Eden' Star Mike Faist on Male Ego, Love Triangles and Still Learning from Steven Spielberg

“You just get bolder and bigger and more confident with time, and you want to be around and work with the right people,” she continued. “And the moment someone is making that vibe feel off, everybody feels it. I don’t want to deal with messy. It’s just about surrounding yourself with professionals who have the same way of working in mind: Show up on time, don’t be rude, don’t be a misogynist.”

Having reached this point in her career, it’s not lost on Pugh the influential position she holds. That’s why she uses her public platform to speak out on matters that are important to her, from Hollywood beauty standards to her support for Palestine . Most recently, she also spoke out against the alleged sexual assault at Cornell University .

The East of Eden star told Elle that she felt compelled to make a statement “because I’m a woman who cares about women.”

“I care about women I know, and I care about women I don’t know,” Pugh said. “And if we allow for stories like that to become in any way normal, then we are allowing ourselves to continue toward that destiny of abuse and rape being accepted as a norm.”

“Rape can never ever be a conversation that we move on from. It has to be something that we look at, face-on, and we demand justice, accountability, and for the rapist to see what they have done to someone’s life. Because if we don’t, we’re accepting it. And I don’t ever, ever, ever want to live in a world where we move on from it easily,” she added.

Congratulations, love y'all,” she commented on the joint post.” Brittany and Patrick’s announcement featured a string of photos of the couple’s children, Sterling, 5, Bronze, 3, and Golden, gathered around their mom by the beach while placing their hands on her belly. “Another blessing from God,” the couple captioned the post. “& then there were 6.” The official NFL and Chiefs Instagram accounts shared congratulatory words in the comments section, while fellow Chiefs star Travis Kelce’s official “New Heights” podcast account also wrote “Congratulations” and added four heart emojis. entertainment.body:

Brandy and Monica are back for more, and taking their hit show to Vegas.

Hot off last year’s sold-out, co-headlining “ The Boy Is Mine Tour ,” the Grammy-winning singers are heading to Resorts World Las Vegas for a 10-date residency that kicks off in May. The singers revealed the news during a special Grammy-themed episode of Dancing With the Stars Tuesday evening (Nov. 10).

Produced by The Black Promoters Collective, The Boy Is Mine Vegas Residency will bring Brandy and Monica to Sin City for a “major new production showcasing their individual catalogs, shared musical history and the timeless songs that have connected generations of fans,” according to press materials.

Tickets for The Boy Is Mine Vegas Residency go on sale to the general public on Friday, Nov. 20 at 10:00 a.m. PT at AXS.com . An American Express presale goes live on Nov. 16 followed by an artist presale Nov. 18.

For Monica, the Vegas residency is an organic continuation of the Boy Is Mine tour, which saw the R&B singers reunite on stage to celebrate their chart-topping single, while performing fan favorites from their respective deep catalogs.

“I realized that people had this really genuine love and excitement for the two of us reconnecting in a musical way,” Monica tells Rolling Stone . “It made me look forward to rehearsals and everything that we were doing. And each time we’d present something to fans, they would fully support it.”

Though the tour ended in December 2025, Monica said she and Brandy continued talking about what they could do together next. That’s when Brandy presented the idea of a stint in Vegas. “I always just loved her passion for us as a brand and ‘Bronica’ as a whole,” Monica says. “And when she brought it to me, I loved the idea so much, because being stationary for me is such an incredible thing, because I have such an in-depth bond with my children, that it gives me the opportunity to be in one place, and they can join me and see me in one space, consistently night after night.”

sports.title: Fran Tarkenton raves about Kirk Cousins's return to Minnesota
sports.summary: On Monday night, I was explaining to my wife the bizarre situation in Minnesota, where a championship-caliber defense has been paired with an offense that would have trouble scoring a touchdown in the lower divisions of college football.
sports.body:
Actually, he is. And the end result to the expedited search came from the Tarkenton playbook: The Vikings brought back a former Vikings quarterback in trading with the Raiders for Kirk Cousins.

On Tuesday, Tarkenton gushed about the return of Cousins. “I think it’s the greatest thing that could have happened to us ,” Tarkenton told Darren Wolfson of KSTP. “We were lost. We were winning on defense. We had no offense. We had no quarterback. And now we’ve got Kirk coming back, who is having a great year. He’s a great player. He’s a better person than player. Our team should lift up now. And we’re in the best division in football. Our defense has kept us in the hunt.

“And having Kirk — I cannot tell you how happy I am for the Vikings, for the fans, for the Wilfs, and for all the players and the old-timers like myself. We’ve got a chance with Kirk Cousins.”

Tarkenton spent 1961 through 1966 with the Vikings before returning from 1972 through 1978. And, as it turns out, his comments about Cousins weren’t the only news he made this week.

Tarkenton apparently earned a mere $1.2 million during his entire 18-year NFL career. But that was just the starting point. He has amassed enough of a fortune in the business world to recently buy — at age 86 — a $51.89 million home in Palm Beach .

Tarkenton blazed the trail for today’s former quarterbacks who work even harder in retirement. He was the first NFL player to host Saturday Night Live , and his TV career included a co-hosting gig on That’s Incredible and a four-year stint in the Monday Night Football booth.

The big money came in the business world, specifically computer software. He also has made many millions as an early investor in Apple.

And, if you watch the clip, you’ll see that Tarkenton still has a verbal and mental fastball.

This is football, man. Especially in the trenches. It gets rough and rowdy. . . . Did you see that big guy, number 50 [Vita Vea], launching at us? . . . It is what it is. We signed up for this.”

“They all do it. It is what it is. You’ve got find ways to combat it,” he said.

It really is anything goes when it comes to line play, subject to what the officials see and are willing to call. Especially when there are so many uncalled holding penalties on offensive linemen, arguably since defensive ends are so good and the powers-that-be prefer to keep quarterbacks in one piece.

The best, most recent example of that came in Carolina on Sunday, on the play when Broncos linebacker Nik Bonitto forced a fumble by Panthers quarterback Bryce Young to seal the game. Bonitto was being held the entire play . And he still got it done.

That’s the message for all offensive and defensive linemen. Do whatever you have to do to get it done. It’s only a foul if a flag is thrown.

sports.body:
The latest betting odds have the Rams as -130 favorites to miss the playoffs, and +110 underdogs to make the playoffs.

That represents a massive shift from before the season, when the Rams were -500 favorites to make the playoffs, the best playoff odds of any team in the league.

The Rams are a disappointing 5-4, and if the playoffs started today they’d be a game behind the Packers for the third and final NFC playoff spot. They’re also 2.5 games behind the 49ers in the NFC West race.

Perhaps more importantly, injuries are mounting for the Rams, with the latest big one being that wide receiver Puka Nacua is heading to injured reserve, where he’ll join Davante Adams, as Matthew Stafford is running out of healthy receivers.

If the Rams get healthy and make the playoffs, they’ll be a major threat to any postseason opponent, which is why they still have the seventh-best odds in the league to win the Super Bowl at +1300.

But as the 49ers pull away in the NFC West, and the NFC wild card race looks increasingly competitive, the Rams’ chances of being in it in January are dwindling.

sports.title: CBA allows 49ers to not pay Brandon Aiyuk during two-week roster exemption
sports.summary: When unusual situations emerge in the NFL, it becomes a piece-by-piece exercise in figuring out the specific rules that apply.
sports.body:
He’s back on the 49ers, at a salary of $13.75 million for the rest of the season. That fact pointed to the 49ers releasing him by 4:00 p.m. ET on Tuesday, in order to avoid owing him one-ninth of the total amount ($1.52 million) for Week 10.

But here’s where yet another obscure wrinkle applies. Under Article 20, Section 4 of the Collective Bargaining Agreement, the 49ers owe Aiyuk nothing during his two-week roster exemption.

From the relevant provision: “If a Club obtains a roster exemption for a player under contract who does not report to his Club at least five days before the final day of Preseason Training Camp as defined in Article 23, Section 10, the player will not be entitled to preseason or regular season compensation until such exemption is removed, provided the player is given written notice of such fact upon reporting to the Club. If such notice is not given to the player, the player must be paid his Paragraph 5 Salary during his exemption.”

So if the 49ers gave Aiyuk written notice that he won’t be paid during the two-week roster exemption (and they surely did), they don’t have to pay him. Which pushes their deadline for avoiding owing him a game check until Tuesday, November 24 — one day after the expiration of the exemption.

Why not just cut him? The 49ers are delaying the move because they can, postponing by up to two weeks his passage through waivers and, given his salary, inevitable free agency.

In the interim, he’s on the team. But Aiyuk won’t be reporting for work on Wednesday. He has been excused, we’re told, from team activities and he’s working out on his own.

The 49ers could release him at any moment. There’s no reason not to do so, other than to apply the brakes to his ability to join another team.

The circumstances counter the notion that he was reinstated by the league subject to any type of agreement with the 49ers. If that had happened, the agreement surely would have included a requirement that the 49ers promptly cut him.

sports.title: Nick Sirianni denies giving subtle middle finger to fans

sports.body:
Sirianni was asked about the apparent gesture during a Monday press conference.

“When [senior vice president of communications] Bob [Lange] told me that, absolutely not,” Sirianni replied. “That was a surprise to me, but absolutely not.”

Frankly, what else would Sirianni say? “Yes, it was a middle finger.” If he admits it, he’ll be fined — and the precedent for coaches is $100,000 .

Beyond that, why would anyone believe him? Last Friday, Sirianni admitted that he misled reporters regarding the team’s supposed commitment to quarterback Tanner McKee.

There’s one other relevant factor, based on my own personal experience. My dad used to use that exact same move, during periodic verbal household disagreements with my mom.

I saw it. She never did. But that was the move. And, if she’d seen it, he would have denied it.

sports.title: In Kirk Cousins, the Vikings landed their first choice

sports.body:

The Vikings explored other options. Multiple players, including fellow former Vikings quarterback Daniel Jones.

Cousins’s history with the team makes it easier to get him up to speed. He had 25 regular-season games with coach Kevin O’Connell, and four seasons with receiver Justin Jefferson.

The existence of options may have helped the Vikings keep the compensation to only a third-round pick. Given the level of desperation, the Vikings seemed destined to give up more than that to fix a problem that threatened to implode the season.

That’s not an overstatement. The dam was breaking. Frustration was rampant during the debacle against the Bills, on both sides of the ball.

It was a simple proposition. If the Vikings didn’t trade for a quarterback on Tuesday, they could not be considered a serious franchise.

In the end, they managed to stop the bleeding by sending their third-round pick (their own, not the one they acquired from the Eagles for defensive end Jonathan Greenard) to the Raiders for Cousins.

It’s unclear how much better things will be with Cousins back in the fold. It can’t get worse than what they put on the field for Week 9.

sports.title: Jaguars-Ravens averages 13.96 million on Prime Video
sports.summary: When it comes to interpreting press releases regarding the audiences for sporting events, there's a rule of thumb.
sports.body:

For the Week 9 Thursday night game between the Jaguars and Ravens— which was destined to have a non-stellar audience thanks to the Ravens being down to their third-string quarterback — Prime Video led with the fact that the eight-game season-to-date average has outperformed last year’s numbers.

The 33-10 win by the Jaguars, which Prime Video accurately called “lopsided” in the release, generated an average of 13.96 million viewers.

It nevertheless was, as Prime Video notes, a 13-percent bump over last year’s Week 9 Thursday night game. And for good reason. The Week 9 Thursday night game in 2025 featured the Ravens at the Dolphins, a 28-6 Baltimore win.

Even with an audience of less than 14 million in the eighth TNF game of the season, the package is offering 17.15 million per week for 2026.

This week’s game — Commanders at Giants — should do well, given that the Giants are both doing well and occupy the nation’s top market. In Week 11, it’s Colts at Texans. Which won’t be great.

The following week, Prime Video has a potentially massive game on Black Friday between the currently 7-2 Broncos and 6-2 Steelers.

After that, it’s Chiefs-Rams, Vikings-Patriots, 49ers-Chargers, Texans-Eagles (on Christmas Eve), and Ravens-Bengals.

sports.title: John Spytek: First "real" call on Kirk Cousins came this morning
sports.summary: As NFL trades slip into hibernation until March, it's important to remember something the next time players can be sent from one team to another.
sports.body:
Teams push plenty of BS to the media — and the media often passes it along without scrutiny.

Case in point: The internally inconsistent claim made by ESPN on Saturday, undoubtedly based on information straight from the Raiders.

“As of this weekend,” Adam Schefter of ESPN tweeted, “the Raiders had not received any trade inquiries regarding their starting quarterback Kirk Cousins, nor are they interested in dealing him , per league sources. They plan to keep sticking with him until they believe their No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza is ready.”

So the Raiders hadn’t received any trade inquiries, but they weren’t interested in the trade inquiries they hadn’t received? Right.

In a press conference with reporters on Tuesday, Raiders G.M. John Spytek addressed how it all came to be.

“I never made one call on Kirk Cousins,” Spytek said. “And I got a few phone calls. But one real one this morning.”

The “real one” ultimately entailed getting a third-round pick for Cousins. Which further highlights how silly it is for a team to claim — and for the media to share — the idea that “WE’RE NOT INTERESTED.”

Everyone is interested in a trade offer for all but a small handful of players in the entire league. Anything else is posturing. And, as is often the case when it comes to NFL reporting, the insiders allow themselves to become extensions of the team’s P.R. department in an effort to send a given message.

sports.title: Malik Nabers: I felt like it was a lie for Fox broadcast to attack my character
sports.summary: "Don't tell the world something that's not me."
sports.body:
Fox announcers Joe Davis, Greg Olsen, and Pam Oliver discussed Nabers’s body language at several points during the game and shots of an agitated Nabers on the sideline were shown multiple times. Davis was particularly critical about Nabers’s response to a touchdown by teammate Isaiah Likely and Olsen said in response that “there’s a very fine line between being demanding, being a competitor, and all those great things” before adding that Nabers has “just got to keep it in check.”

Nabers responded to those comments and misattributed quotes that claimed Olsen called him a bad teammate in a social media post after the 19-11 win over the Eagles. Nabers said the broadcast tried to “create a narrative” that wasn’t true and shared more thoughts on the matter Tuesday.

“I just feel like the narrative on me is always all the bad body language things that people have been saying about me,” Nabers said, via a transcript from the team. “But as far as that, if it’s a problem with anybody, the cameras can stay off me. The thing about it is, don’t tell the world something that’s not me. I’m [going to] speak up for myself all the time because there’s nobody else that’s going to be able to speak up for me. So, I’m going to use my own voice and be able to speak up about me being a bad teammate. And I felt like that was just a lie, just attacking my character as a football player and as a teammate. Like I said, I’ve never been on a team where anyone has called me a bad teammate that I know of.”

Olsen took issue with the incorrect quotes about Nabers being a bad teammate and the wideout was asked if he’s heard from directly from him since Sunday. Nabers said he hasn’t, but “he can reach out and we can have a simple conversation.” Beyond that, Nabers said he’s done talking about the subject and that he’s moved on to Thursday’s game against the Commanders.

sports.body: A year after making a pair of franchise-altering deals at the NFL trade deadline, the Jets stayed quiet this year. The only trade they made was a minor one, sending backup safety Andre Cisco to the Detroit Lions in exchange for a future sixth round pick. The Jets did not trade defensive end Will McDonald despite McDonald requesting a deal to a new team and other teams reportedly having interest. At 2-7, there would be no way to justify this team being a buyer. So we ended up with a trade deadline that lacked much activity for this team.

sports.title: Buffalo Bills fans grade the trade for safety Amani Hooker
sports.summary: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Bills fans and fans across the country. Buffalo Bills president of football operations/general manager Brandon Beane did it again, tackling one of the team’s biggest roster needs
sports.body: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Bills fans and fans across the country. Buffalo Bills president of football operations/general manager Brandon Beane did it again, tackling one of the team’s biggest roster needs just hours before the 2026 NFL trade deadline. It represents a move that most of Bills Mafia have been banging the folding tables for going on weeks now, due to the often confused assignments and play observed out of Buffalo’s defensive secondary. The deal for Hooker also reveals another savvy move by Beane to leverage all layers of quality in negotiating a trade. Specifically, Buffalo sent a 2027 second-round pick to the Titans in return for Hooker and a fifth-round pick. One Bills Drive was also rumored to have been looking into making a trade for safety Budda Baker of the Arizona Cardinals, but Arizona’s front office relented. Many Bills fans were concerned when they found out Buffalo hadn’t pulled off a trade with the Atlanta Falcons to land safety Jessie Bates, instead watching him head to the Jacksonville Jaguars. Despite that concern, it’s now clear that Beane was working the phones to improve the Bills’ roster, and it’s a deal that looks better on paper compared to what Jacksonville gave up to get Bates. Hooker is younger than Bates, and he’s a player who gives the Bills more roster control at the position while spending less capital to acquire him, as outlined by Matt Warren. Hooker currently leads the NFL with five interceptions, three of which came in one game against quarterback Joe Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals. sports.title: The Kirk Cousins contract points to a revised deal or termination after 2026
sports.summary: The last time the Vikings brought back a key former player for a third-round pick, the reunion didn't last long.
sports.body:
In 2010, the Vikings sent a third-round pick to the Patriots for receiver Randy Moss, whom the Vikings had traded to the Raiders in 2005. Former coach Brad Childress, calling Moss a “programmatic non-fit,” released Moss after four games.

Now, quarterback Kirk Cousins returns for a third-round pick, and a contract that covers nine regular-season games. His deal with the Raiders was structured to maximize the amount the Falcons owed Cousins for 2026 ($8.7 million, on top of the $90 million he made in 2024 and 2025) with another $10 million paid by the Raiders to Cousins in 2027, in the form of a guaranteed roster bonus not subject to offset.

The contract also includes a 2028 base salary of $78.655 million that becomes fully guaranteed on the fifth day of the 2027 league year. Coupled with a $1.345 million base salary in 2027 that becomes fully guaranteed that same day, the Vikings would be on the hook for $80 million over two years if he’s not released by then.

Without a revised deal, the current contract surely would be torn up by March. The question is whether the Vikings and Cousins would be able to come up with a new contract to replace it.

Much of that depends on how the rest of the year goes. Still, Cousins has the ability to force his way to free agency, for the fourth time in his career, by simply declining to re-do the existing deal.

However it plays out, Cousins can be counted on to make a good business decision. He has $333 million in career earnings, which has him at fourth on the all-time list .

On-field success is a different story. He has made it to the postseason three times in his career, with one playoff win.

If, as expected, the return of Cousins provides a B-12 shot to the Minnesota franchise, he has a realistic chance of getting back to the playoffs. And of winning a second postseason game.

sports.summary: Josh Downs has gotten his wish.

Kansas City will receive Downs and a 2027 seventh-round pick in exchange for 2027 fourth- and fifth-round picks.

sports.title: Chargers trade Daiyan Henley to Broncos for 2027 fourth, 2028 fifth-round picks
sports.summary: The last-place team in the AFC West is trading a player to the first-place team in the AFC West.
sports.body:
The Chargers have traded linebacker Daiyan Henley to the Broncos for a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick.

For the Broncos, it’s an addition of a linebacker who has started every game but one for the Chargers over the last three seasons, and should be able to step in and contribute immediately in Denver.

For the Chargers, it’s an addition of two draft picks for a winless team that desperately needs to build for the future. Henley is in the final season of his rookie contract as a 2023 third-round pick and might have left the Chargers this offseason anyway. Now the Chargers are getting something for him.

Henley is a defensive captain, and there were reports that the Chargers weren’t looking to trade important players, but realistically, when you’re the worst team in the league, you’re going to trade players for picks if a good offer comes your way.

Some teams prefer not to trade with division rivals, but in this case, it’s a trade that should benefit both teams, so there’s no reason for both teams not to do it. And now Henley will attempt to win the AFC West this season, something he was not going to do in Los Angeles.
