sports.body: The Buffalo Bills have allowed 16 total points the past two games, but the unit has certainly faced lesser competition at quarterback. How much should we take from Buffalo’s recent defensive efforts? Is it all a mirage because they faced one snap of Lamar Jackson, only a few attempts from Tyler Huntley, then Joey Fagnano, Carson Wentz, and Max Brosmer? Or is Buffalo really onto something defensively? These type of questions are precisely why I created Defensive Impact on Passing (DIP). I introduced the new metric a few weeks ago, and if you missed that article, here’s how I can summarize DIP — it measures how well a defense performs against opposing quarterbacks relative to how those same quarterbacks perform against other defenses on their schedule. Pretty straightforward right? Baked into DIP is the exclusion of garbage time, and, like all EPA-based defensive stats, a negative figure is better. Also, quarterbacks need at least 30 attempts against other opponents to be counted toward a defense’s DIP. sports.body: The Andre Cisco era is over for the New York Jets. Actually, that’s a misnomer. These days we seem to always designate something an era that in no way merits the term. Andre Cisco falls firmly in that category. The New York Jets have traded backup safety Andre Cisco to the Detroit Lions for a 2028 sixth round draft pick. That’s better. The Jets originally acquired Andre Cisco by signing him as an unrestricted free agent in 2025. Cisco was brought in expecting to be a playmaker in the back end of the defense, but it did not work out that way. After eight weeks of uninspired play in 2025 in which Cisco racked up zero interceptions, one pass defended, one tackle for loss and one fumble recovery, with little in the way of defensive playmaking, Cisco’s 2025 campaign ended with a season ending injury. The Jets let his contract expire in 2026 and Cisco explored free agency before the Jets brought him back on a one year, $2.2 million deal. He was expected to compete with Dane Belton for the safety spot opposite Minkah Fitzpatrick, but Belton is clearly the better player. Fitzpatrick missed time early in the season, opening up playing time for Cisco, but Cisco did little with the opportunity. Once Fitzpatrick returned to action Cisco was relegated primarily to special teams play. Over parts of two seasons Andre Cisco played 17 games for the Jets, starting 12. He racked up a total of 64 tackles, one sack, two passes defended, one forced fumble, three tackles for loss and one fumble recovery with the Jets. Cisco allowed an abysmal 115 passer rating in coverage during his time with the Jets. The trade of Cisco opens up playing time for 2025 fourth round draft pick Malachi Moore in the short run. 2026 seventh round pick V.J. sports.body: Over the last several weeks, we have seen the classic unraveling of a Jets season. The faces change, but the results always seem to stay the same. Entering Week 7, the Jets faced a two game homestand against beatable opponents. Victories against both the Dolphins and the Raiders would get the team to .500 through eight games and give this team real momentum heading into a tough stretch facing the Chiefs and Bills back-to-back. Of course, the Jets handed the previously winless Dolphins their first victory and then lost to the Raiders, dropping their record to 2-6. Not even at the halfway point, the season was over. It is normal for the competitive portion of the season to end early for Jets fans. It feels like an annual tradition in November to be discussing NFL Draft position above all else. The only thing the Jets still had going for them is it felt like the team was still united. Players were fighting for each other. Things changed in the Week 9 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs. The Jets looked like an imploding team. Fans could see it in obvious ways like Minkah Fitzpatrick making a couple of business decisions when he had opportunities to make plays. Armand Membou threw his helmet in frustration in an emotional outburst after allow a second half sack. Geno Smith was demonstrative in his frustration frequently as the game slipped away. These are symptoms of a season that is slipping away and a team that is in a spiral. Through each offseason NFL fans of all 32 teams convince themselves that their team has made all of the right moves, and their roster is improved. That’s part of being a fan. At this time of year, Jets fans frequently are forced to confront the reality that the team made bad moves in the previous offseason, and that has a lot to do with the team’s struggles. The Jets might not have gotten everything wrong in the 2026 offseason. David Bailey increasingly looks like a budding star. If the two pass catchers the Jets took in the first round of the NFL Draft after Bailey aren’t dominating, they at least look promising. Still, at this point I think the obvious is staring Jets fans in the face. This remains a bottom tier roster, and many of the offseason moves that provided hope in March were poor decisions in hindsight, particularly on the defensive side of the ball. And on offense, the internal improvements fans hoped for just haven’t been as big
